n: About thirty years later, John the Baptist appears preaching in the Judean desert near the Jordan River. He was Jesus’s relative, born six months before Him.

f.g: Decades after chapter 2; JST adds details of Jesus growing up and waiting upon the Lord.
The dry hill country east of Jerusalem, sloping to the Jordan and Dead Sea.

n: His message: “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near!” To repent means to turn — change your mind, heart, and direction.

f.g: Greek metanoeō — to change one’s mind and turn around.
Matthew’s usual phrase for the kingdom of God; Jews often avoided saying God’s name directly.

n: John is the voice Isaiah foretold, crying in the wilderness to prepare the Lord’s way and make His paths straight.

f.w: The voice of one crying in the wilderness

n: John wore camel-hair clothing with a leather belt and ate locusts and wild honey — simple desert food. His dress resembled the prophet Elijah’s.

f.g: Grasshoppers, permitted as food under the law (Leviticus 11:22).

n: Crowds came from Jerusalem, all Judea, and the Jordan region.

f.g: The river running from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea.

n: They were baptized by John in the Jordan, openly confessing their sins.
When Pharisees and Sadducees came, John called them a brood of snakes: “Who warned you to flee coming judgment?” He sees through religious show.

f.g: A strict Jewish party devoted to detailed obedience to the law and oral traditions.
A priestly, aristocratic party that rejected the resurrection and oral law.

n: Show real repentance by the way you live — produce fruit that matches it.
Don’t rely on being Abraham’s descendants; God could make children of Abraham from these stones. Covenant blessings depend on faithfulness, not ancestry.

f.w: We have Abraham to our father

f.g: In Aramaic/Hebrew a likely pun: “stones” (abanim) and “sons” (banim).

n: The axe is already at the root of the trees; every unfruitful tree will be cut down and burned. Judgment is near.

f.w: the axe is laid unto the root of the trees
every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit

n: John baptizes with water for repentance, but One more powerful is coming — whose sandals John isn’t worthy to carry. He will baptize with the Holy Ghost and fire.

f.w: whose shoes I am not worthy to bear
f.g: Carrying sandals was a servant’s lowliest task.

f.w: with the Holy Ghost, and with fire

n: Like a farmer with a winnowing fork, He will clear His threshing floor, store the wheat in the barn, and burn the chaff. He will separate the faithful from the unfaithful.

f.g: A winnowing fork, used to toss grain so the wind blows away the chaff.

n: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.
John objects: “I need to be baptized by You, and You come to me?” He recognizes Jesus’s greater holiness.
Jesus answers: “Let it be so now; it is right for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Though sinless, Jesus was baptized to obey the Father and show the way. Nephi explains this beautifully.

f.w: Suffer it to be so now

n: Coming up out of the water — showing baptism by immersion — Jesus saw the heavens open and the Spirit of God descend like a dove upon Him.

f.w: went up straightway out of the water

n: The Father’s voice declares, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.” All three members of the Godhead are present and distinct: the Son baptized, the Spirit descending, the Father speaking.
